title: Prejudice & Stereotypes Adventure
welcome_lead: Snap judgments about whole groups — that's prejudice. ⚖️
meta_desc: Social Psychology Adventure 3 — KS3 Psychology on prejudice, stereotypes and reducing them.
final_note: You learned about stereotypes, prejudice and ways to reduce them.

concepts.def: Fixed belief about a whole group
Spending time with another group reduces bias

walkthroughs.body_html:
A stereotype is a fixed belief about a whole group.

Even 'positive' stereotypes ('all X are good at maths') can be unfair to individuals.

Prejudice = feeling. Discrimination = action.

Refusing to be friends with someone because of their religion is discrimination.

Psychologist Gordon Allport found contact reduces prejudice — when groups meet as equals.

Tips:

  • Mix in clubs and teams.
  • Learn each other's stories.
  • Call out unfair jokes.

Real people beat stereotypes every time. 🤝

mcqs.q: Allport said the best way to reduce prejudice is…

options: Just grabbing whoever is around (any haphazard method).
Every member of the target population has an equal chance of selection.
Picking participants who match the population profile.
